message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** (Alfred Hitchcock) | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1978 | **The Shining** (Stanley Kubrick) | Atmospheric dread, iconic imagery, and a chilling performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 1984 | **The Thing** (John Carpenter) | A tense, claustrophobic alien invasion with groundbreaking practical effects. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** (Jonathan Demme) | A psychological thriller with unforgettable characters. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** | Pioneered the found‑footage style and created a new wave of horror. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** (Danny Boyle) | Fast‑moving, post‑apocalyptic horror that revitalized the zombie genre. |
| 2004 | **Saw** (James Wan) | Dark, twisted, and full of moral dilemmas. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Low‑budget found‑footage that still delivers genuine scares. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (James Wan) | A modern classic that blends folklore with supernatural terror. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (Dennis Dugan) | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and frightening. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” concept with a haunting soundtrack. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** (Robert Eggers) | A slow‑burn, atmospheric period horror that’s unsettling in subtle ways. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** (Jordan Peele) | A socially conscious horror that’s as clever as it is scary. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** (John Krasinski) | Tension built around silence, with a strong family dynamic. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** (Ari Aster) | A daylight horror that’s both beautiful and disturbing. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** (Leigh Whannell) | A modern retelling of a classic tale with strong feminist themes. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** (Nia DaCosta) | A fresh, culturally relevant take on a horror legend. |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** (Scott Derrickson) | A supernatural thriller with a unique premise and strong performances. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** (David Gordon Green) | A horror‑comedy about a murderous AI doll that’s both creepy and funny. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—psychological, supernatural, slasher, or something more experimental. Enjoy the chills!
